reader.notes: RecordDelimiterNames holds the two implementor-names (GnuCOBOL's, per the R13 precedence) and each selects a documented method (docs/conformance/7/DOC-A.1-151); the file bytes match. LINE-SEQUENTIAL makes the file line sequential at 85 as well (FileModel.LineSequentialByDelimiter), which is the method the implementor associates with that name.

refuter.evidence: Probe refute-1985-238/rdely.cob (runs/rdely-001) at --std 85 (rdelx.cob, the X"0A" form, is refused at 85 COBOL0900 as a 2002 literal, so the LF byte comes from SYMBOLIC CHARACTERS LFC IS 11). ORGANIZATION SEQUENTIAL + RECORD DELIMITER IS LINE-SEQUENTIAL: OPEN I-O 00, READ 00 06, REWRITE 00, re-read 'UNO   ' 06 and 'TWO' 03: the sequential file keeps its I-O mode and its lengths. But a legal 5-character variable-length record 'AB'+LF+'CD' WRITE gives I-O status 71 ('LFW 71'), nothing written ('LF1 10'). The method the implementor associates with LINE-SEQUENTIAL cannot determine the length of a record that holds the delimiter character, and the failure is reported with 71, a value 1985 does not define: §1985:VII.1.3.5 lists 00-49 and confines implementor conditions to 9x (the same arm gives 06 and 09 on READ, also not 1985 values). The path consults no edition: the LINE-SEQUENTIAL name sets FileModel.LineSequentialByDelimiter at every edition and the runtime takes the 2023 line sequential arm (§2023 '71' rule) wholesale. Reading for UPHELD: GR3 leaves the method wholly to the implementor, and DOC-A.1-115's line character set is that method's documented domain, so the 71 is a defect of the 1985 I-O status rule, not of GR3. Reading for OVERTURNED: GR3 with GR1 ('Any method used will not be reflected in the record area or the record size used within the program') requires the method to determine the length of every legal variable-length record, and this one restricts record content. No kb/Work note found (grep for 71 with 1985). cite.py: OK  §1985:VII.2.8.4 GR3 the text is in GR3; OK  §1985:VII.2.8.4 GR1 the text is in GR1. OK  §1985:VII.1.3.5 the text is in the clause; it lies in GRL2.5a ('I-O Status = 9x ... must not duplicate any condition specified by the I-O status values 00 through 49').
